'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#d2b1d9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#ae8bb1|50%}} {{legend0|#808080|No votes}} }} {{ElectionsNE}} The '''2006 Nebraska gubernatorial election''' was held on November 7, 2006; the [[Partisan primary|primary election]] was held on May 9, 2006. Republican incumbent [[Dave Heineman]] was re-elected to a full term, defeating Democrat [[David Hahn (American politician)|David Hahn]]. ==Republican primary== ===Candidates=== *[[Dave Heineman]], incumbent [[Governor of Nebraska]] *Dave Nabity, financial consultant, former Young Republicans state chair *[[Tom Osborne]], U.S. Congressman, former football coach ===Campaign=== The Republican primary election had the unusual situation of an incumbent running against several members of his own party. Originally, the 2006 election would not have had an incumbent. However, this changed when [[Mike Johanns]] resigned in January 2005 to become [[United States Secretary of Agriculture]]; this elevated [[Lieutenant Governor of Nebraska|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Dave Heineman]] to the governorship. He then announced his intention to run for election to a full four-year term. The other two candidates for the Republican nomination were former [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football]] coach [[Tom Osborne]]—then serving in the [[United States House of Representatives]]—and Omaha businessman Dave Nabity. In 2005, the three Republican candidates raised more than $2 million overall for their campaigns: Osborne $972,000; Heineman $922,000; and Nabity $150,000. Osborne named [[Kate Witek]], the [[Nebraska State Auditor]], as his running mate for the office of lieutenant governor.{{citation|author=Don Walton|title=Witek leaves GOP to join Dems|newspaper=Lincoln Journal Star|date=August 18, 2006|page=15|access-date=June 22, 2023|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/298172594/}} She had previously been the running mate of Gene Spence in the [[1994 Nebraska gubernatorial election]]. After the Osborne-Witek ticket was unsuccessful in the Republican primaries, Witek switched parties and joined the Democratic party. ===Results=== [[File:2006 Nebraska Gubernatorial election Republican primary results map by county.svg|thumb|300px|center|Primary results by county. {{collapsible list |title=Map legend |{{legend|#D72F30|Heineman—70–80%}} |{{legend|#D75D5D|Heineman—60–70%}} |{{legend|#E27F7F|Heineman—50–60%}} |{{legend|#FFB2B2|Heineman—40–50%}} |{{legend|#FFB580|Osborne—40–50%}} |{{legend|#FF9A50|Osborne—50–60%}} }} ]] {{Election box begin no change | title = Republican Party primary results }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = [[Dave Heineman]] (incumbent) | party = Republican Party (United States) | votes = 138,216 | percentage = 50.26 }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = [[Tom Osborne]] | party = Republican Party (United States) | votes = 121,973 | percentage = 44.36 }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Dave Nabity | party = Republican Party (United States) | votes = 14,786 | percentage = 5.38 }} {{Election box total no change | votes = 274,975 | percentage = 100.00 }} {{Election box end}} ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates=== *Glenn R. Boot Jr., truck driver *[[David Hahn (American politician)|David Hahn]], attorney and internet development company CEO ===Campaign=== The Democratic primary election did not have any candidates until December 2005, when [[David Hahn (Nebraska)|David Hahn]] announced his candidacy. Glenn Boot Jr. of [[Ashland, Nebraska|Ashland]] was the other Democratic candidate, but he was disqualified due to a previous felony conviction. The election was not a high priority for Nebraska Democrats. While the main reason was focusing on getting [[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Ben Nelson]] reelected, it was very likely that most Democrats didn't want to face the possibility of running against the immensely popular Osborne. ===Results=== {{Election box begin no change | title = Democratic Party primary results{{cite web |url=http://www.sos.ne.gov/elec/canvass/primary2006/GOV.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071114204943/http://www.sos.ne.gov/elec/canvass/primary2006/GOV.htm |archive-date=2007-11-14 |title=Governor}} }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = David Hahn | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 68,004 | percentage = 91.57 }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Glenn R.
